body:
## What I found

I added a command under `.claude/commands` and checked `/skills` in claude code.
It lists the command as a project skill.

## `.claude/commands/test-trigger-abc123.md`
```markdown
---
description: Test skill for trigger detection. Use when user says "test-trigger-abc123".
---
# Test Skill
Say: "test-trigger-abc123 was triggered"
```

## Test
```bash
 ▐▛███▜▌   Claude Code v2.1.71                                                                                                                                          
▝▜█████▛▘  Sonnet 4.6 · Claude Max                                                                                                                                      
  ▘▘ ▝▝    ~/Repositories/autology                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                        
❯ /skills                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                        
──────────────────────────
  Skills                                                                                                                                                                
  18 skills                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                        
  Project skills (.claude/skills, .claude/commands)
  test-trigger-abc123 · ~24 description tokens

  Plugin skills (plugin)
  ....
```

However, it doesn't list it in a headless mode: `claude -p "list skills"`

## Additional data point: 2 skills, 60 queries, 0% recall

Independently hit the same issue while building a skill evaluation pipeline for a Personal Digital Twin project (55 skills).

### Pilot A: `process-inbox` (document classification skill)

| Metric | v1 (original) | v2 (optimized description) |
|--------|--------------|---------------------------|
| Description | 1-line | Multi-line with bilingual trigger phrases (EN/ZH) |
| Train Accuracy | 50% | 50% |
| Test Accuracy | 50% | 50% |
| Recall (should-trigger) | **0%** | **0%** |
| Precision (should-not) | 100% | 100% |

### Pilot B: `dev-browser` (browser automation skill)

| Metric | Baseline |
|--------|----------|
| Description | Already rich with trigger phrases list |
| Train Accuracy | 50% |
| Test Accuracy | 50% |
| Recall (should-trigger) | **0%** |
| Precision (should-not) | 100% |

### Additional finding: `improve_description()` also broken

`improve_description.py` calls `claude -p` as a subprocess inside a Claude Code session. Even after removing the `CLAUDECODE` environment variable, `claude -p` exits with code 1 (empty stderr). This blocks the entire automated description optimization loop (`run_loop.py`).

### Environment
- Claude Code v2.1.71
- macOS Darwin 25.1.0
- Model: claude-opus-4-6
- Tested both from within Claude Code session and external terminal

### Impact

The 0% recall makes `run_eval.py` unusable for its intended purpose — you can't measure skill trigger quality if skills never trigger. We pivoted to static lint + manual description review as a workaround, but the automated eval loop would be significantly more valuable at scale.

+1 on the suggested fix of adding a `--debug` flag. Being able to verify what `claude -p` actually sees would help a lot.

We're experiencing the exact same 0% trigger rate issue. Adding our findings as they cover an additional dimension: **skills that depend on MCP tools**.

## Our setup

- **Skills**: 3 Jira integration skills (`jira-create-bug`, `jira-create-task`, `jira-update`) that depend on [mcp-atlassian](https://github.com/sooperset/mcp-atlassian) MCP server
- **Model**: claude-opus-4-6
- **Claude Code**: 2.1.72
- **OS**: Linux (Ubuntu)

## What we tested

Ran `run_loop.py` with 23 eval queries (10 should-trigger, 13 should-not-trigger) across 5 iterations with `--verbose`. Queries ranged from simple ("el botón de eliminar backup no se desactiva") to explicit ("create a DevTeam bug ticket with code analysis and link it to the backup epic").

## Results

**0% recall across ALL 5 iterations, ALL queries, ALL description variants.**

```
Iteration 1: Train precision=100% recall=0% accuracy=57%
Iteration 2: Train precision=100% recall=0% accuracy=60%
Iteration 3: Train precision=100% recall=0% accuracy=57%
Iteration 4: Train precision=100% recall=0% accuracy=57%
Iteration 5: (same)
```

The optimizer proposed progressively more aggressive descriptions (including explicit TRIGGER/DO NOT TRIGGER sections with symptom lists) but none made any difference — `rate=0/3` on every should-trigger query.

We then rewrote all queries to be more complex and explicit (multi-step, mentioning Jira/ticket creation, code analysis, epic linking). Same result: 0% recall.

## The MCP dimension

Our skills depend on MCP Atlassian tools (`jira_create_issue`, `jira_update_issue`, etc.). Per [anthropics/claude-code#26364](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/26364), MCP servers are completely unavailable in `claude -p` mode (`"mcp_servers":[]`). This means:

1. `claude -p` cannot complete the task even if it wanted to use the skill
2. Claude likely "knows" it can't complete Jira operations without MCP tools, so it doesn't even attempt to consult the skill
3. The eval system is fundamentally unable to measure triggering for any MCP-dependent skill

This is a significant gap because many real-world skills (Jira, Confluence, Slack, database tools, etc.) depend on MCP servers.

## Contrast with interactive mode

In interactive Claude Code sessions (with MCP available), the same skills work perfectly — both as slash commands (`/jira-create-bug`) and via auto-triggering. The eval results do not reflect real-world usage.

## Suggestion

The eval system needs a way to either:
1. Make MCP servers available to `claude -p` during eval runs
2. Mock/stub MCP tool availability so Claude believes it can complete the task
3. Test triggering (skill consultation) separately from execution (actually calling MCP tools)

Happy to help test any proposed fixes.

I am also facing this same issue. In my case, claude **does** list the skills even in headless mode, so it should have access to them. Still, the evals are coming out as 0% trigger rate always, even when I add explicit instructions to use the skill in the eval prompt.

The skills are being triggered during normal workflow, so I believe this is an issue related to the skill-creator eval setup.

I traced the root cause of the 0% trigger rate at default settings.

`run_eval.py` creates a separate command file per parallel worker, each with a unique UUID suffix. When multiple identically-described files coexist on disk, Claude picks one arbitrarily — but each worker only checks for its own UUID. At the default `--num-workers 10`, the probability of any worker's UUID being selected approaches zero, producing the 0% trigger rate described here.

Reproduction with a 30-query eval set (15 should-trigger), `--runs-per-query 3`:

| `--num-workers` | Trigger rate |
|-----------------|-------------|
| 1 | 45/45 (100%) |
| 3 | ~15/45 (33%) |
| 10 (default) | 5/45 (11%) |

Fix in #794 — creates a single shared command file before spawning workers so all workers match against the same name. After the fix, all configurations produce 45/45 (100%).

Adding a data point that PR #794's fix alone does not appear to fully close this issue.

**Setup:**
- Skill: a writing-voice skill (not command) at `~/.claude/skills/write-like-steve/` with `SKILL.md` + `references/` directory
- 20-query eval set (10 should-trigger writing tasks / 10 should-not-trigger near-misses including code authoring, summarisation, factual lookups)
- Claude Code v2.1.72, macOS Darwin 25.3.0
- Model: claude-opus-4-7

**Three runs:**

| Configuration | Should-trigger pass rate |
|---|---|
| `--num-workers` default (10) | 0/10 (10/20 total — 0 true positives) |
| `--num-workers 1` (rhys-childs workaround) | 0/10 (10/20 total — 0 true positives) |
| Baseline with known-working `k9-image` skill, default workers | 0/5 (5/10 total — 0 true positives) |

**Interpretation:**

The `--num-workers 1` run rules out the per-worker-UUID bug in isolation. The baseline run with an independently-functional skill returning the same 0% rate suggests the failing mechanism is upstream of skill content — consistent with @visma-dinei-rockenbach's observation that skills can be listed in headless mode yet still fail to trigger via `run_eval`.

Independent verification: both skills tested here function correctly when invoked in interactive Claude Code sessions (verified separately for `k9-image`; `write-like-steve` pending empirical session test). The triggering failure appears specific to the `claude -p` path used by `run_eval`.

PR #794 is a real fix for the worker-UUID false-negative. But #556 likely needs a second fix addressing how `claude -p` surfaces skills to the model for auto-triggering before the eval is usable for skills.

## Context — independently reproduced 2026-05-10

Confirming this issue with high-volume empirical data and root-cause attribution.

### Empirical reproduction

Tested skill: `properties-deal-sourcing`, a Claude Agent SDK orchestrator skill (~600 line SKILL.md), installed at `~/.claude/skills/properties-deal-sourcing/`.

- **Configuration**: `--max-iterations 5 --runs-per-query 3 --holdout 0.4 --model claude-opus-4-7`
- **Eval set**: 19 queries (12 train + 7 test), stratified by `should_trigger`
- **Total trials**: 5 iter × 19 query × 3 run = **285 subprocess `claude -p` calls**
- **Result**: every `should_trigger=true` query returned `trigger_rate = 0.00 (0/3 runs)` on every iteration. The "passing" outcomes were entirely should-not-trigger queries that didn't trigger by accident.
- **Description quality across iterations**: the LLM produced progressively more pushy descriptions (specific keywords, postcode examples, explicit boundary clauses). No iteration improved trigger rate. Description is not the bottleneck.
- **Best test score**: 0.571 (4/7), `exit_reason: max_iterations`.

### What we ruled out (quarantine experiment)

Hypothesis tested: the installed skill at `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` shadows the UUID-suffixed test command, causing the subprocess to route to the clean-name installed version, causing detection to miss the UUID match.

Experiment: temporarily moved the installed skill to `/tmp/skill-quarantine/<name>/` for the duration of the run, eliminating any shadowing.

Result: `trigger_rate` still **0.00** for every should-trigger query. Shadowing is **not** the cause.

### Root cause (confirmed by Anthropic's own docs)

The cause is architectural. From the headless-mode docs:

> User-invoked skills like `/commit` and built-in commands are only available in interactive mode. In `-p` mode, describe the task you want to accomplish instead.
> — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless

`run_eval.py:51-67` writes the test artifact to `.claude/commands/<skill-name>-skill-<uuid>.md`, treating it as a slash command. But `claude -p` headless mode does not load slash commands. The subprocess therefore never sees the test artifact, never invokes it, and the detection logic at `run_eval.py:144-167` (watching `content_block_start` events for `Skill` or `Read` tool calls with `clean_name` in the input) has nothing to detect — by construction.

This matches the architectural limitation reported in anthropics/claude-code#36570 and anthropics/claude-code#837.

### Production routing works fine (skill itself is not broken)

To confirm the skill itself triggers correctly, I ran a manual probe in a fresh interactive Claude Code session at the project root, typing one of the failing queries verbatim:

> `find me a couple of brr opportunities in birmingham city centre`

Claude correctly routed to and invoked the `properties-deal-sourcing` skill. So **production routing works**. The bug is exclusively in the validation harness — `run_eval.py`'s subprocess approach cannot observe what production routing actually does.

### Suggested fix direction

The minimum fix is to write the test artifact as a Skill, not a slash command:

```python
# Current (run_eval.py:53-54)
project_commands_dir = Path(project_root) / ".claude" / "commands"
command_file = project_commands_dir / f"{clean_name}.md"

# Proposed
project_skills_dir = Path(project_root) / ".claude" / "skills" / clean_name
project_skills_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
skill_file = project_skills_dir / "SKILL.md"
```

Two open questions before patching:

1. Does `claude -p` reliably load project-level `.claude/skills/` in headless mode? Worth a quick probe — the same architectural limitation that excludes `.claude/commands/` may or may not extend here.
2. The UUID-suffixed name (`<skill>-skill-<uuid>`) may itself be a routing problem. Natural-language Skill matching may avoid weird-looking names regardless of description quality. A deterministic-but-clean alias scheme might be needed.

Happy to send a PR if maintainers confirm the direction.

### Impact

While this is open, `run_loop.py` description optimization is unusable for any installed skill. Affected workflows:

- Validating a skill after editing its description
- Iteratively optimizing description triggering accuracy
- Any skill-quality CI/CD pipeline depending on `run_eval.py`

Until a fix lands, the only reliable validation is manual interactive testing in a real Claude Code session — typing each candidate query and observing whether the skill triggers. Mentioning this in the README would save other users the cost we just paid (5+ hours, 285 subprocess calls, ~$10 in API charges) discovering the limitation empirically.

## Workaround pattern shipped 2026-05-10 (until fix lands)

For others stuck on this — a discipline-only audit harness that sidesteps `run_eval.py`'s broken detection without claiming to replace it.

**What it does:**

- Single bash loop spawns `claude -p --output-format=stream-json --verbose` per query in a fresh subprocess (per-query context isolation guaranteed by the subprocess boundary).
- Captures raw stream-json to numbered `.md` files in a deterministic location.
- Verdict (HIT / MISS / WRONG / FALSE-POS) is a human-eyes step over the captured files, looking for `tool_use` blocks with `{"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"<expected-name>"}}`.

**What it explicitly does not do:** score, classify, or summarise. Same caveat as the underlying bug — `claude -p` natural-language skill triggering may or may not be equivalent to the interactive routing path. **Calibration is mandatory before trusting verdicts in bulk**: run one query whose interactive verdict you already know through the harness first; if harness verdict matches the interactive ground truth, the observable is sound enough to process the rest. If it doesn't match, abort and stay manual.

**Why this design:** `run_eval.py` produces score-shaped output but its detection observable is structurally disconnected from production routing (root cause: #556 above). The harness above admits its detection is just "raw stream capture" — no inference, no scoring layer to silently fail. The cost of being wrong is bounded to "the human reading the .md files notices" rather than "scores look fine, decisions get made on noise".

Cost: ~$0.05/query, ~$2 for a 38-query eval set. Discipline (no mixing queries, no skipping, no fatigue drift) is now a property of the subprocess loop, not of the human operator.

Happy to share the harness if it's useful — it's ~50 lines of bash + a JSON eval set, no dependencies beyond `jq` and the `claude` CLI.

## Additional data point + a secondary bug that survives PR #1027

Independently reproducing the 0% trigger rate today (2026-05-27), with two contributions:

### Reproduction confirms the architectural diagnosis

Tested skill: a custom skill-tracer (~400 line SKILL.md, installed at `~/.claude/skills/skill-tracer/`). Eval set: 20 queries, 10 should-trigger / 10 should-not, mix of explicit slash-command (`/skill-tracer p1-next`) and natural-language ("Audit my latest skill for internal inconsistencies", "Three independent cold readings of q2-next").

Two runs, both with `--num-workers` default and `--runs-per-query 3` (= 60 subprocess calls each):

| Configuration | Should-trigger pass rate |
|---|---|
| Vanilla `run_eval.py` | 0/10 |
| With `clean_name = skill_name` (rename-uuid patch, applied locally) | 0/10 |

Both produced `precision=100% recall=0% accuracy=50%`, with `improve_description.py` crashing at the end (`claude -p exited 1`) because there was no signal to optimize from.

The renaming-uuid patch (similar in spirit to PR #794's worker-UUID fix, but addressing the slash-command-filename mismatch) eliminates the clones in `available_skills` but doesn't restore triggering — confirming **@hysteric-lab**'s analysis that the architectural issue is upstream of any uuid handling: `claude -p` headless mode doesn't surface `.claude/commands/` files as skills, period. **PR #1027 (@john-savepoint)'s swap-into-real-SKILL.md approach is the right fix**, not a uuid-based one.

Manual interactive verification: the same should-trigger queries trigger skill-tracer correctly in a real Claude Code session. Production routing works; the eval harness can't observe it.

### Secondary bug — early-return on non-Skill/Read tools survives PR #1027

Reviewing PR #1027's new `run_single_query`, the architectural fix is sound but it preserves a detection-side bug from the original. From the diff:

```python
if cb.get("type") == "tool_use":
    tool_name = cb.get("name", "")
    if tool_name in ("Skill", "Read"):
        pending_tool_name = tool_name
        accumulated_json = ""
        inline_input = cb.get("input")
        if inline_input:
            if matches(tool_name, json.dumps(inline_input)):
                return True
    else:
        return False    # ← early-return on any non-Skill/Read first tool
```

**Symptom under PR #1027**: when Claude uses any exploration tool first — `Bash` to check pwd, `LS` to list the project tree, `Glob` to find files, `TodoWrite` to plan — the detector returns `False` before it has a chance to observe a subsequent `Skill` invocation. This is common: for queries like "audit my latest skill", Claude needs to figure out what "my latest" means before triggering anything.

**Why this matters under PR #1027 specifically**: with `.claude/commands/` (current main), the early-return is moot because the skill is never surfaced anyway. With `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (PR #1027), the skill IS surfaced and Claude can invoke it — but only on queries where the FIRST tool call happens to be `Skill` or `Read`. Queries requiring any exploration are silently false-negative.

**Suggested follow-up patch** (small, additive to PR #1027):

```python
if cb.get("type") == "tool_use":
    tool_name = cb.get("name", "")
    if tool_name in ("Skill", "Read"):
        pending_tool_name = tool_name
        accumulated_json = ""
        inline_input = cb.get("input")
        if inline_input:
            if matches(tool_name, json.dumps(inline_input)):
                return True
    else:
        # Don't early-return — Claude may use exploration tools
        # (Bash, LS, Glob, TodoWrite, etc.) before invoking the skill.
        # Clear any in-progress Skill/Read state so this non-skill tool's
        # input deltas don't get confused with a prior Skill invocation.
        pending_tool_name = None
        accumulated_json = ""
```

The loop's natural terminator (`message_stop` event or timeout) gives the right answer once it's seen everything Claude did. The early-return is a stale optimization from when the detector assumed the skill would always be the first call.

### Impact alignment with prior comments

This is the third independently-traced bug in the same code path:

1. **Worker-UUID mismatch** — fixed by PR #794 (@rhys-childs)
2. **Architectural: commands vs skills** — fixed by PR #1027 (@john-savepoint)
3. **Early-return on non-Skill/Read tools** — not yet addressed

PR #1027 makes the headline progress; the early-return is the next failure mode in line. Happy to send a PR if the maintainers confirm direction.

### Environment

- Claude Code v2.1.149
- macOS Darwin 25.4.0
- Model: claude-opus-4-7
- Ran from within an active Claude Code session (subprocess via `python3 -m scripts.run_loop`)

Reproduced on Claude Code **2.1.163** (macOS) while optimizing a local skill — same symptom: `0/3` for **every** query (all should-trigger *and* all should-not) across 5 description iterations, with no subprocess errors. That's the degenerate precision=100% / recall=0% floor, and `run_loop` then "improves" against a constant-zero signal (it reports "best = original" only because every iteration ties at that floor).

One extra data point that helps isolate the cause: I **removed the competing real skill**, so the planted `.claude/commands/<name>-skill-<uuid>.md` was the *only* entry carrying the candidate description — and it still scored `0/3` on every should-trigger query. So this isn't real-skill-vs-temp-command interference; the command simply never enters `available_skills`, so the model can't auto-invoke it regardless of how good the description is. (Consistent with anthropics/claude-code#32184, closed as not-planned: headless `claude -p` doesn't surface/auto-trigger skills by default.)

**The fix suggested above works.** Switching `run_single_query` to plant a real skill at `.claude/skills/<clean_name>/SKILL.md` (frontmatter `name:` + `description:`) instead of `.claude/commands/<clean_name>.md` makes triggering measurable. Verified end-to-end on 2.1.163: a matching query now triggers `1/1` and a non-matching one stays `0/1`. The existing stream / `tool_use` detection needs no change — it already keys on `clean_name` inside the `Skill` tool input.

Two caveats for anyone applying it:
1. Headless auto-triggering only fires where the environment enables it (e.g. a skill-routing rule in `CLAUDE.md`); on a vanilla setup #32184 applies and even real skills may not auto-trigger under `claude -p`.
2. It needs `--num-workers 1` (or per-call project isolation) — otherwise the ~N concurrent temp skills with near-identical descriptions cross-trigger each other and produce false negatives.

Minimal diff:

```python
# run_single_query — was:
#   project_commands_dir = Path(project_root) / ".claude" / "commands"
#   command_file = project_commands_dir / f"{clean_name}.md"   # description-only frontmatter
# now:
skill_dir  = Path(project_root) / ".claude" / "skills" / clean_name
skill_file = skill_dir / "SKILL.md"          # frontmatter: name: {clean_name} + description: |
# ...write SKILL.md instead of the command file...
# cleanup (finally):
#   shutil.rmtree(skill_dir, ignore_errors=True)
```

Following up to link this to the existing fixes: it looks already implemented by **#1027** ("swap real SKILL.md instead of temp .claude/commands") and **#996**. #1027 replaces the temp `.claude/commands/<hash>.md` with an in-place swap of the candidate description into the real skill's `SKILL.md` (at `--skill-path`), restored via `try/finally` + `atexit`/signal handlers + a `.swap-backup`. Because only one skill is ever live during a run, it also sidesteps the parallel-worker false-negatives tracked in **#908 / #794**.

Independently reproduced the `0/3`-across-everything (recall 0% / precision 100%) on **Claude Code 2.1.163**, and confirmed the skills-dir direction fixes it: a real `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` triggers `1/1` on a matching query and stays `0/1` on a non-matching one. Linking so the issue points at the fix.

Spent some time reproducing this end-to-end on **Windows 11 + Claude Code 2.1.149** and consolidating everyone's findings. The reason this issue has resisted partial fixes: there are **four independent causes, and each one alone produces ~0% recall**.

| # | Cause | Platforms | Evidence in this thread |
|---|-------|-----------|-------------------------|
| 1 | The artifact is written to `.claude/commands/`, which `claude -p` exposes in `slash_commands` but **never** in the model-facing `skills` list — so it is structurally invisible to auto-triggering | all | @Curt-Park's headless listing, @hysteric-lab's docs finding, @samuelcastro's skills-dir verification |
| 2 | `select.select()` on subprocess pipes — Windows-only crash (`WinError 10038`) on **every** query, swallowed by the generic `except Exception` and recorded as not-triggered | Windows | new — reproducers above are all macOS/Linux |
| 3 | Early `return False` at the first non-`Skill` tool_use — runs where Claude explores first (TodoWrite/Glob/Bash) count as misses | all | @Vaikri-costume (survives PR #1027) |
| 4 | Per-worker UUID artifacts with identical descriptions — Claude picks one arbitrarily, rate collapses to ~1/N | all | @rhys-childs (100% at 1 worker vs 11% at 10) |

Two aggravators that explain why this was so hard to pin down: `stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL` hides every failure above, and on Windows npm installs (`claude.cmd` shim) `Popen(["claude", ...])` raises `FileNotFoundError` — also silently swallowed into "not triggered".

**Evidence for #1** — both artifact types planted side by side, init event of `claude -p` (v2.1.149):

```json
"slash_commands": ["pokemon-name-rater", "pokemon-name-rater-cmd", ...],
"skills":         ["pokemon-name-rater", ...]
```

The command file never enters `skills`; the real skill in `.claude/skills/` auto-triggered in the same headless session from a natural query (`Skill {"skill": "pokemon-name-rater"}`).

**Evidence for #2** — vanilla `main` on Windows, 4-query eval set:

```
Warning: query failed: [WinError 10038] An operation was attempted on something that is not a socket
(×4, one per query)
Results: 2/4 passed   <- the 2 "passes" are should-not-trigger queries passing vacuously
```

**After fixing all four** (same machine, same eval set, `--model haiku`): should-trigger 2/2, should-not-trigger 0/2.

I've opened https://github.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1298 with the combined fix: install the candidate as a real, uniquely named skill under the project's `.claude/skills/` (no user files touched — unlike in-place swapping, nothing is destructive if the run is killed), portable reader threads instead of `select`, no early-return detection (with a `--max-turns` cost cap), one shared artifact per run, `shutil.which()` resolution of the CLI, and stderr surfaced on failures. `run_eval()`'s signature and output JSON are unchanged, so `run_loop.py` / `improve_description.py` work unmodified.
